title: Ulla bar Chinena—or Chananyah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Sukkah 33a and 36a and in Nazir 51b, under the formula “Ulla b-Ch (ב״ח) taught.”

notes.text: The words בשם הני in the frozen notice remain unclear. The shortened ב״ח is expanded only from the explicit alternative patronymics Chinena/Chananyah; no extra authority or statement is invented.

The saved named Davidson Sukkah 33a and Nazir 51b paragraphs explicitly use תני, “recited/taught,” with Ulla bar Chinena and Ulla bar Chanina respectively. They support a contextual teaching-formula comparison, not proof that supplied הני was printed תני. The source בשם הני remains unresolved; heading Chananyah is distinct from the Nazir witness’s Chanina. The supplied Sukkah 36a occurrence was not newly checked.

Hyman (vol. III, p. 975) prints the teaching formula בשם תני, where the supplied text has בשם הני. The Davidson texts at Sukkah 33a, Sukkah 36a and Nazir 51b all have תני. Sukkah 33a names Ulla bar Chinena; the other two name Ulla bar Chanina. Hyman’s alternative in the heading is Chananyah. The abbreviated ב״ח is kept.
